tasks.title: roster shows join state, and owner-admins get invite / re-send / withdraw
tasks.redPrompt:
Write the FAILING suite for #294. Contract = `cd ~/workspace-app && gh issue view 294 --comments` — READ THE COMMENTS, they amend the body substantially. The body's central premise (that an admin cannot read another member's redemption state, and that this 'gates the whole feature') was DISPROVED by live probe and is superseded. Research: `teams/mvox-dev/memory/research/research-294.json`. Drift-check every line number — #287 just landed in this same file.

## The state model — discriminate on CONTENTS, never on presence
Three states, read from the person's `entu_user` property:
- **never invited** — no `entu_user` entry at all
- **invited, not redeemed** — an entry carrying `invite` (masked `'***'` on every read after the mint), no `uid`
- **joined** — an entry carrying `uid`/`provider`/`email`, never `invite`

A PRESENCE check (`has entu_user` vs not) classifies an invited-but-never-joined member as JOINED — which is precisely the population the controls exist for. A spec that tests presence rather than contents is wrong in the only case that matters. Pin this explicitly.

## Who sees what — PO ruling 2026-09-09 (issuecomment-5591996566), verified
- **Display of the three states: EVERY admin** (`admin === 'admin'`, i.e. `_owner` OR `_editor` on the database entity per `adminStore.ts:84-85`). A `_viewer`-level read already returns the placeholder shape, so an editor-admin loses nothing.
- **The three controls: `_owner` ONLY.** Live probe (`scripts/migrations/probes/probe-294-admin-invite-cascade-2026-09-09.ts`): an `_owner` on the database entity CAN mint onto another member's person (HTTP 200); an `_editor` CANNOT (HTTP 403, Entu's text: `"User not in _owner property"`).
- **An editor-admin gets ONE LINE where the controls would be**, saying invites require owner rights. NOT three disabled buttons, NOT three failing buttons, NOT silence. Pin all three negatives.

## The controls, by state
- never invited → `kutsu` (invite)
- invited, not redeemed → `saada uuesti` (re-send) AND `tühista kutse` (withdraw)
- joined → no controls

`kutsu` reachable on a person who already has a live link is a STATE-ROUTING BUG, not a case to handle. Pin that it is unreachable there.

## Invariant to pin — one person, at most one redeemable link, at any moment
PO ruling. Minting a second link while one is live is forbidden. Verified live: Entu APPENDS — a bypass mint left TWO live placeholders — and entu-api's `findStoredInvite` returns the FIRST entry carrying any `invite` WITHOUT checking it against the token presented at redemption. So an older token stays independently redeemable. **Gama's demanded test, write it: after `saada uuesti`, the previously issued link must no longer redeem.** Test the invariant, not the button.

## `tühista kutse` is a REVOCATION, not tidiness — two properties are load-bearing
1. **A bound identity must NEVER be touched.** The sweep filters on `invite` being present; a joined member carries `uid` and never `invite`. Pin that withdraw cannot unlink someone who has actually joined.
2. **Partial failure IS failure. All-or-report.** Multiple placeholders can coexist and the sweep loops. A surviving placeholder is a live credential the admin has just been told is dead. Pin: if any DELETE fails, the operation reports failure — never a partial success rendered as done.

## Withdrawn and never-invited are the SAME state — Mihkel ruling, do not add data to separate them
After a withdrawal the truthful state is 'no live credential exists', identical to never-invited, and the available action is the same. A withdrawn person REAPPEARS in the 'needs inviting' population and that is correct, not a wart. Pin the collapse; do not pin any marker distinguishing them.

## Do NOT use the profile entity as a join proxy
Ruled out with evidence: a profile entity is created on first profile SAVE, not at login (`applyProfileSave.ts:60`), so a person who joined and never edited their profile has none. That signal would report exactly the target population as not-joined.

## Existing behaviour to leave alone
`listActiveMembers` (`rosterData.ts:118-127`) THROWS when a member has no readable `person` reference, failing the whole collective's roster load. That is deliberate fail-loud, it is a DIFFERENT field from `entu_user`, and it is out of scope. Do not soften it. It also means a person-less member can never render as a row, so there is no such state to build a control for.

## Do not assert the token lifetime
Source says `expiresIn: '7d'`; #23's thread measured 24h live. Unresolved — no spec may assert either number.
tasks.greenPrompt:
Implement #294. Contract = issue body AS AMENDED BY ITS COMMENTS (read them; the body's rights premise is superseded). Research = `teams/mvox-dev/memory/research/research-294.json`. Probe = `scripts/migrations/probes/probe-294-admin-invite-cascade-2026-09-09.ts`. Drift-check all lines — #287 just landed in `roster/+page.svelte`.

**(1) Reading join state needs an ADDITIONAL fetch.** Neither roster-load query projects `entu_user`: `listActiveMembers` requests `props=person,_parent` (`rosterData.ts:102-108`) and `listProfilesForPerson` requests `props=name,email,_sharing`. `entu_user` lives on the PERSON entity and every existing call site reads it as `entity/{personId}?props=entu_user` (`inviteData.ts:379`, `linkedIdentities.ts:53`). Fan out per row with `Promise.all`, mirroring the profile fan-out `loadRoster` already does (`rosterData.ts:347-352`).

**(2) REUSE `listLinkedIdentities`** (`linkedIdentities.ts:46-79`) — it is already generic over any `personId` and already performs the exact uid-vs-invite-vs-absent split. Its only current caller passes the caller's OWN personId; that is a call-site fact, not a limitation of the function. Do not write a second discriminator.

**(3) `saada uuesti` REUSES `mintSelfLinkInvite` as-is** (`inviteData.ts:371-463`) — probe-confirmed to work for an `_owner` caller against another person, no library change needed. It already does read → sweep stale `invite`-carrying entries → mint, in that order.

**ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING — sweep BEFORE mint, never the reverse.** Entu has no transactions, so 'one action' cannot be atomic. Mint-then-failed-sweep leaves TWO live links and breaks the invariant the whole feature rests on. Sweep-then-failed-mint leaves ZERO, which is recoverable via `kutsu` and is the safe failure direction. `mintSelfLinkInvite` already orders it correctly — preserve that, and do not 'optimise' it.

**(4) `tühista kutse` does NOT exist yet.** It is `mintSelfLinkInvite`'s sweep WITHOUT the mint (`inviteData.ts:395-415`: read `entu_user`, filter entries carrying `invite`, `DELETE /property/{_id}` each). Extract the sweep into its own exported function and have BOTH call it — do not duplicate the loop. Two properties must survive the extraction: a bound identity (carrying `uid`, never `invite`) is never selected; and a partial failure is a failure, reported as such, never rendered as done.

**(5) Gate the controls on the RIGHTS FACT, directly.** `adminStore.ts:84-85` collapses `_owner` and `_editor` into a single `'admin'` state, so it cannot express this on its own. Surface owner-ness specifically. **Do NOT build a general owner/editor capability layer** — PO ruling: one boundary is not a role system, and there is a parked roles-versus-rights question this must not pre-empt. Smallest change that expresses the one fact.

**(6) A 403 must surface as a NAMED error**, never a control that silently does nothing.

**(7) i18n — all four locales.** New keys for three state labels, three control labels, and the editor-admin owner-rights line. Keys stay VOCABULARY-NEUTRAL (skin-neutrality rule: domain vocabulary lives in message VALUES, never in keys, component names, or types). Estonian values are given in the issue (`kutsu`, `saada uuesti`, `tühista kutse`); supply en/lv/uk equivalents. Match the naming convention of neighbouring `roster_*` keys. Reuse any existing invite-related key rather than duplicating.

**(8) Do NOT touch** `listActiveMembers`' fail-loud throw on a missing `person` reference — different field, out of scope, deliberate.

**STATED-CHOICE DISCIPLINE** (sentences in result summary AND commit body): (a) how owner-ness is surfaced and why it is not a capability layer; (b) where the sweep was extracted to and how both callers share it; (c) how partial-failure-is-failure is enforced in withdraw; (d) how the editor-admin line renders and confirmation no disabled control ships alongside it.

Full suite green (`pnpm test`, PATH=~/.local/share/pnpm:$PATH) and `pnpm check` clean.
tasks.reviewChecklist:
LETTER-FIRST against #294's comment-amended contract. The body alone is NOT the contract — verify against the comments.
1. CONTENTS NOT PRESENCE: the discriminator reads `uid` vs `invite` from `entu_user` entries. Any test for the property's mere presence classifies invited-but-not-joined as joined — the exact population the feature exists for. FINDING if presence is used anywhere.
2. RIGHTS SPLIT: display for every `admin`; the three controls for `_owner` only. Probe-established (`_editor` gets HTTP 403 'User not in _owner property'). Display gated on owner is a FINDING; controls shown to an editor-admin is a FINDING.
3. EDITOR-ADMIN TREATMENT: exactly one line saying invites require owner rights. THREE DISABLED BUTTONS IS A FINDING — this page had that class of lying affordance removed in #273 and #286, and re-adding it in the same release would be indefensible. Silence is also a finding.
4. NO CAPABILITY LAYER: owner-ness expressed as the one rights fact it is. A general owner/editor role/capability abstraction is a FINDING regardless of elegance — PO ruled it pre-empts a parked question.
5. ONE LIVE LINK: verify sweep happens BEFORE mint and that this ordering is preserved, not reordered. Mint-before-sweep leaves two live links on partial failure and breaks the invariant. Verify the demanded test exists: after re-send, the previously issued link no longer redeems.
6. WITHDRAW IS A REVOCATION: (a) a bound identity carrying `uid` can never be selected by the sweep — a joined member must be un-unlinkable; (b) partial failure reported as failure. A surviving placeholder is a live credential the admin was told is dead. Either missing is a FINDING.
7. SWEEP EXTRACTED, NOT DUPLICATED: one implementation shared by re-send and withdraw. A copied loop is a FINDING — it will drift, and both copies are security-relevant.
8. COLLAPSE HONOURED: withdrawn and never-invited are indistinguishable, by ruling. Any marker, flag, or schema addition preserving the distinction is a FINDING.
9. NO PROFILE PROXY: join state must not be inferred from profile-entity existence — a joined member who never edited their profile has none, and would be misreported as not-joined.
10. i18n: all new keys present in en/et/lv/uk, keys vocabulary-neutral, values carrying the domain words. A missing locale or a vocabulary-bearing key is a FINDING.
11. NO SCOPE CREEP: `listActiveMembers`' throw on a missing `person` reference untouched.
12. NO LIFETIME ASSERTION: no spec or comment asserts 7d or 24h — the discrepancy is unresolved.
13. NO REGRESSION: the full existing roster suite green, including #287's collective-switch specs which landed in this same file immediately before.
tasks.commitBody: The roster now says whether each member has actually joined, and owner-admins can act on it. Join state is read from the contents of the person's `entu_user` — an entry carrying `uid` means joined, one carrying a masked `invite` means invited and waiting, and no entry means never invited. Reading mere presence would have called every invited-but-never-joined member joined, which is the whole population the controls exist for. Every admin sees the state; only an `_owner` gets the controls, because a live probe established that an `_editor` cannot mint onto another member's person at all — so an editor-admin gets one line explaining that invites need owner rights, rather than three buttons that would 403 on every click. Re-send reuses the existing sweep-then-mint path unchanged, preserving its ordering: Entu has no transactions, and sweeping after minting would leave two independently redeemable links, which is the failure the one-live-link rule exists to prevent. Withdraw is that same sweep without the mint, extracted so both callers share one implementation — it can never touch an identity that has actually joined, and a partial sweep reports failure, because a surviving placeholder is a live credential the admin has just been told is dead. Withdrawn and never-invited deliberately collapse into one state, per ruling. STATED CHOICES: <GREEN agent fills the four stated choices as sentences>.
